What mfrmr Calculates and Where to Read More

Source: R/help_methods_reference.R
mfrmr_methods_reference.Rd

Locate the calculation and literature for a chosen question. This is a help topic, not a function. Use the model-choice tutorial to select a model and mfrmr_workflow_methods to connect analysis steps.

Distinguish the target

A Person ability, a rater severity, observed agreement and a G coefficient answer different questions. A facet is a modeled role (Rater or Task); its levels are individual raters or tasks. More facets do not mean more ability dimensions. Prespecify the score, population, rating unit and intended comparison before choosing a calculation.

TargetDefinition and implementation
Ordered-response model, estimator, scale and anchorsfit_mfrm_technical_details: RSM/PCM/GPCM, MML/JML/CML, identification, weights and numerical approximation
Information in the observed assignment and categoriesdescribe_mfrm_data(), subset_connectivity_report(): retained rows, support and design review
Structural uncertaintymfrm_facet_intervals(), mfrm_population_intervals(): target, covariance/interval method and conditions
Conditional ability scores or plausible valuespredict_mfrm_units(), sample_mfrm_plausible_values(), mfrm_calibration_score_methods
Response fit, ZSTD, separation and residualsdiagnose_mfrm() for supported ordinary models; mfrm_response_diagnostics() for supported extended models
Category use, steps and probability curvesrating_scale_table(), mfrm_report_category_structure, mfrm_report_category_curves
Conditional bias and group contrastsestimate_bias(), analyze_dff(), mantel_haenszel_table(), ordinal_logistic_table()
Observed agreementinterrater_agreement_table(), pairwise_icc_table(), pairwise_kappa_table(), krippendorff_alpha_table(), gwet_ac2_table()
Assessment-plan variance and precisionmfrm_g_study(), mfrm_d_study() and their covariance/interval methods
Score classificationclassification_table() and fixed-calibration decision methods in mfrm_calibration_workflow

The linked help is the reference for the implemented equations, denominators, defaults, output columns and original sources. A general model citation does not by itself justify an implementation choice or extension.

Choose an agreement target and keep its denominator

Match the same rated response by its Person/Task/Criterion keys. Exact agreement counts matched pair-context opportunities; its model-expected counterpart is not chance agreement in kappa or AC2. Pairwise kappa uses each pair's common complete units. Alpha and AC2 pool ratings differently, including their treatment of singleton units and category distances. Read the selected helper's denominator before comparing values. ICC additionally requires an interval-score interpretation and choices of agreement/consistency, selected/random raters and single/average ratings. A pair's average-rating ICC concerns two raters, not the whole panel.

These raw-score helpers supply descriptive points and counts, without sampling intervals; save their complete lists with saveRDS(). They are separate from the fitted mfrm_interrater summary/plot bundle. Repeated responses from one Person are not automatically independent; high agreement does not establish accuracy against a defensible reference.

Distinguish rater effects before choosing a diagnostic

Severity concerns generally higher/lower ratings after model adjustment. Centrality concerns compression toward middle categories; use rater_centrality_table(), not graph centrality. Halo/horn concerns impression spillover across criteria: rater_halo_network_analysis() describes score associations, not their psychological cause. A negative edge does not identify a horn effect. Local dependence concerns variation shared beyond the fitted model; a supported fit_mfrm_testlet() model represents a declared shared effect without identifying its cause. None of these mechanisms is diagnosed by Infit/Outfit alone. Direct FM-SC/MRFM-H models are not implemented; the specialist help distinguishes them from these descriptive routes.

Choose the G-theory target and uncertainty

Score columns are fixed score components, not additional random facets or latent dimensions. Choose the uncertainty target before the method:

TargetInterface
A source variance/covariance componentconfint.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy()
Joint sampling covariance of component estimatesvcov.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy()
A future plan's G, Phi or measurement SEMconfint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study()
A difference between plans using the same sourceconfint(d, reference = 1, ...) or mfrm_d_study_comparison

A coefficient's sampling SE differs from measurement SEM. Paired plans need their shared-source covariance/set, not subtraction of marginal endpoints. The linked methods require explicit normal-model assumptions and their documented design/estimator conditions; incomplete source data do not authorize sparse future plans. Current D-studies project complete balanced plans.

summary(d) returns point coefficients; intervals = TRUE requests supported uncertainty and retains separate IntervalCenter values where applicable. Keep original estimates, status and notes: negative components, out-of-range delta limits, empty sets and numerical failures have different meanings. REML centers are not MINQUE estimates, and pointwise ribbons are not simultaneous bands. Method comparison is sensitivity analysis, not a coverage study. The separate mfrm_generalizability() main-effects approximation has residual sensitivity, not confidence intervals. Use the G-theory tutorial for a worked interpretation and the specialist help for formulas and limits.

Conditions that change interpretation

  • Design: connectedness alone does not identify all joint effects or guarantee precision. Missing assigned scores differ from unassigned cells; using available ratings does not correct informative missingness.

  • Scale and anchors: score direction, facet signs and centering constraints must match. Ordinary fixed-anchor inference conditions on supplied values; propagating source uncertainty requires an explicit supported covariance route. See mfrmr_linking_and_dff.

  • Uncertainty: conditional posterior SD, structural sampling SE and G/D-study uncertainty are distinct. Specify what is held fixed. An available interval does not establish repeated-sample coverage; NA is not zero or an infinite endpoint. Use mfrmr_output_guide("intervals") for the available targets.

  • Diagnostics: residual misfit, bias, dependence and observed disagreement require different follow-up. A flag is not a causal explanation or a verdict on fairness. High rater separation means distinguishable severities, not agreement; low separation can also reflect poor precision.

  • Score combination: G/Phi concern the declared score and replication design. Reliability alone does not justify combining constructs or establish the validity of a use. Changing components, weights or the universe of raters/tasks changes the question.

Find and cite the supporting literature

Read the chosen function's method and reference sections, and report the settings actually used. The sources below introduce the model families and score-interpretation framework; specialist help links its own formulas and adaptations to their sources. Use citation("mfrmr") for the software and record packageVersion("mfrmr").

References

American Educational Research Association, American Psychological Association, & National Council on Measurement in Education. (2014). Standards for educational and psychological testing. American Educational Research Association. Internal structure and score-combination rationale: Standards 1.13–1.14, pp. 26–27; reliability/precision, Chapter 2. https://www.testingstandards.net/uploads/7/6/6/4/76643089/standards_2014edition.pdf.

Kane, M. T. (2013). Validating the interpretations and uses of test scores. Journal of Educational Measurement, 50(1), 1–73. doi:10.1111/jedm.12000 . A framework for claims, assumptions and evidence; not validation of a particular mfrmr calculation.

Andrich, D. (1978). A rating formulation for ordered response categories. Psychometrika, 43, 561-573. doi:10.1007/BF02293814 . RSM foundation.

Masters, G. N. (1982). A Rasch model for partial credit scoring. Psychometrika, 47, 149-174. doi:10.1007/BF02296272 . PCM foundation.

Muraki, E. (1992). A generalized partial credit model: Application of an EM algorithm. Applied Psychological Measurement, 16(2), 159-176. doi:10.1177/014662169201600206 . GPCM foundation.

Bock, R. D., & Aitkin, M. (1981). Marginal maximum likelihood estimation of item parameters: Application of an EM algorithm. Psychometrika, 46, 443-459. doi:10.1007/BF02293801 . Marginal-likelihood estimation framework; this citation does not mean every mfrmr engine uses EM.

Linacre, J. M. (1989). Many-facet Rasch measurement. MESA Press. Many-facet formulation and interpretation.

Wright, B. D., & Masters, G. N. (1982). Rating scale analysis. MESA Press. Fit, separation and reliability conventions.

Linacre, J. M. (2002). What do Infit and Outfit, Mean-square and Standardized mean? Rasch Measurement Transactions, 16(2), 878. https://www.rasch.org/rmt/rmt162f.htm. An introductory fit explanation.

Brennan, R. L. (2003). Coefficients and indices in generalizability theory (CASMA Research Report No. 1). University of Iowa. Pages 3–4 introduce random-facet G/D error and coefficient targets. https://education.uiowa.edu/sites/education.uiowa.edu/files/2026-04/casma-research-report-1-archived.pdf.
